comments.body:
Phase 1 RCA (confirmed before repair): `tests/conftest.py::_remove_readonly_run_snapshots` materializes `tuple(tmp_path.rglob(".rebar/run_snapshots"))`, so it recursively enters every unrelated mutable subtree below a test temp root, including `tests/interfaces/conftest.py::rebar_repo`'s live `repo/.tickets-tracker`. The canonical store write lifecycle intentionally creates and removes `.ticket-write.lock.d` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py` dual-window contract). Python 3.11 `Path.rglob` caches directory entries from a parent scan and catches `PermissionError` but not `FileNotFoundError` when a cached child vanishes before descent; Python 3.12+ delegates to a walk that ignores the same scandir error. A deterministic runtime barrier used the real `rebar._store.lock.acquire`: after the tracker parent scan cached the live mkdir lock, `LockHandle.release()` removed it; the actual fixture teardown then raised the exact `FileNotFoundError` at `.ticket-write.lock.d` on Python 3.11. The identical barrier returned normally on Python 3.12. This proves canonical lock churn plus the broad mutation-intolerant scan and supported 3.11 traversal semantics are sufficient, while a stable tree or 3.11 alone is not.

The competing hypothesis that MCP async completion or the lock lifecycle is defective was rejected. Under a real held lock, direct cleanup of an exact `.rebar/run_snapshots` root succeeded and left the lock intact; only the fixture's broad traversal failed when release occurred mid-walk. Async daemon execution and dual-window lock removal are explicit contracts (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`). Fixture ordering is not causal: direct invocation of the actual fixture reproduced outside pytest fixture scheduling.

Defect legitimacy: Python 3.11 is an explicit supported CI/runtime target (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, `pyproject.toml`), and closed bug `actinium-civic-needletail` requires shared cleanup of every exact `.rebar/run_snapshots` below test-owned `tmp_path` while preserving unrelated content and read-only publication. Commit `bedfb276...` introduced this regression. Expected repair behavior: retain recursive exact-root coverage and tolerate only unrelated entries that disappear concurrently; do not change workflow async semantics, store locking, snapshot permissions, or mask non-disappearance filesystem errors.

comments.body:
Phase 2 final debug report (repair verified; Gerrit landing pending)

Problem: Gerrit 1876 PS2 failed only on Ubuntu/Python 3.11 after 13,892 passes because shared snapshot teardown recursively descended into a canonical tracker mkdir lock that vanished mid-walk.

Proven root cause: `tests/conftest.py::_remove_readonly_run_snapshots` used broad `Path.rglob` across the whole test `tmp_path`; supported Python 3.11 caches child entries and does not suppress `FileNotFoundError` when a cached directory disappears before descent. A real `LockHandle.release()` at the post-parent-scandir barrier reproduced the exact `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock.d` traceback in the actual fixture. Python 3.12 tolerated the identical interleaving. Direct exact-root cleanup succeeded while the real lock remained held, rejecting async MCP and canonical lock lifecycle as defects.

RED/GREEN: the held-out oracle in `tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py::test_snapshot_cleanup_tolerates_disappearing_tracker_lock` creates a real lock, exact snapshot tree, and adjacent file; releases the lock at a deterministic scandir barrier; and invokes the actual root fixture. Final-form Python 3.11 RED was the exact vanished-lock `FileNotFoundError`. The blind fixer never saw the oracle. With the repair it is GREEN, removes the snapshot root, and preserves adjacent bytes. A second control proves `PermissionError` remains visible. Reintroducing the original `Path.rglob` line returned the exact-defect mutation to RED; restoring the repair returned 2/2 GREEN. The oracle asserts observable teardown consequences and is insensitive to helper names/extraction.

Fix: recursive discovery now uses `os.walk(..., onerror=...)`, ignores only `FileNotFoundError` for concurrently vanished entries, re-raises every other walk error, retains arbitrary-depth exact `.rebar/run_snapshots` discovery, and keeps `_rmtree_writable`/read-only publication unchanged. No production code, dependency, workflow lifecycle, or store lock semantics changed; no existing assertion was weakened.

Verification: Python 3.11 focused matrix 30 passed; Python 3.12 focused matrix 29 passed/1 expected version skip. Deterministic barrier passed 25/25 on Python 3.11. The original MCP workflow node passed 10/10 on a proper Python 3.11 environment. CI-shaped broad default gate (`-n 4 --dist worksteal`, non-integration/non-external/non-repo-policy) passed 13,886 with 53 skipped in 15:03. `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `git diff --check` passed.

Caller/safety sweep: the autouse fixture is the only behavioral caller. Existing snapshot producers at `tests/unit/workflow/test_snapshot.py`, `test_prior_art_hardening.py`, and the cross-module cleanup test depend on recursive exact-root coverage, which is preserved. The live tracker/lock and MCP async path are intended behavioral dependencies and were not changed.

Sibling sweep: an AST census of every pytest fixture containing a yield plus `rglob`/`glob`/`walk`/`scandir`, followed by teardown-hook/finalizer searches, found no other live recursive teardown scan; only this repaired fixture matched. Parity axis is N/A: this is a shared pytest lifecycle invariant, not a multi-interface operation.

Residual risk/prevention: none observed without disposition. Python 3.11 carries the deterministic race oracle; later runtimes still execute the non-disappearance error control and the full shared cleanup suite.

Replication: the original failing node no longer reproduced in 10 Python 3.11 runs, and the stronger synchronized lock-release scenario passed 25/25.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
1879 PS1 CI RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1).

Confirmed root cause: the os.walk repair introduced two ambient `Path(dirpath)` factory calls in tests/conftest.py:353,358. The three Windows-simulation tests at tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:163,206,322 monkeypatch `D.os.name="nt"`; src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:20 and tests/conftest.py:22 share the same stdlib os module, and the cleanup fixture tears down before monkeypatch restoration. On supported Python 3.11, pathlib.Path.__new__ consults the live os.name, selects WindowsPath, and rejects it on POSIX. The os.walk dirpath itself is an ordinary absolute POSIX string; the failure is ambient concrete-path selection during teardown, not malformed path data or vanished-lock handling.

CI evidence: run 32198213506 job 95906676612 produced exactly three teardown errors after all three bodies passed; 13,897 other tests passed. Ubuntu/Python 3.12 passed. Local Python 3.11 exact-node reproduction was deterministic: 3 passed + the same 3 teardown errors.

Discriminating proof: immediately before conversion under Python 3.11, os.name=`nt`, `D.os is os` was true, dirpath was a normal `str`, and tmp_path was PosixPath. `Path(dirpath)` raised `NotImplementedError: cannot instantiate WindowsPath`; `type(tmp_path)(dirpath)` succeeded as PosixPath. Driving the cleanup generator with the monkeypatch active reproduced the error; restoring os.name before cleanup completed normally. The minimal version probe reproduced 3.11 error versus 3.12 construction. These outcomes confirm the shared-monkeypatch/factory hypothesis and reject generic os.walk/path corruption, lock-churn/onerror behavior, and permanent traversal corruption.

Defect legitimacy: defect. Python 3.11 is supported by pyproject.toml:16 and the CI matrix; the cleanup contract in tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py requires removable snapshot trees, adjacent-data preservation, and propagation of non-FileNotFoundError scan failures.

Caller-dependency gate: expected post-fix behavior is identical recursive exact `.rebar/run_snapshots` discovery with FNF-only walk tolerance, independent of a test-scoped os.name monkeypatch. The fixture is autouse; its only direct test hook is tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:27. No caller behaviorally depends on ambient Path flavor selection. Phase 2 is unlocked; the repair must preserve os.walk and must not broaden exception masking.

This is one root-cause class with two sequential artifacts, not a rival cause. Exact mutation evidence: restoring both original conftest Path calls makes the held-out oracle RED at conftest.py:358; stabilizing those conversions but removing the scoped snapshot.Path binding makes the same oracle RED at snapshot.py:145; restoring both protections returns GREEN. The fix remains test-harness scoped and preserves `_rmtree_writable` production behavior for every non-test caller.

## Context
Gerrit 1876 patch set 2, GitHub Actions run 32193981982, Ubuntu Python 3.11 job 95894688032 failed after 13,892 tests passed. The session teardown fixture `tests/conftest.py::_remove_readonly_run_snapshots` evaluated `tuple(tmp_path.rglob(".rebar/run_snapshots"))`; traversal entered `repo/.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock.d`, which disappeared during recursion, and `pathlib` raised `FileNotFoundError`. The failing node was `tests/interfaces/store/test_workflow_entrypoints.py::test_mcp_run_workflow_is_async_and_pollable`.

## Plan
- Reproduce the traversal failure with a deterministic barrier while separating three rivals: Python/pathlib version semantics, concurrent mkdir-lock churn, and fixture scope over the whole pytest temp tree.
- Establish defect legitimacy and caller impact from the teardown contract and prior read-only snapshot cleanup bug.
- Design a held-out race oracle at the smallest tier that executes the production teardown helper with real concurrent filesystem mutation; prove final-form RED.
- Repair only the confirmed mechanism, then prove held-out GREEN, exact-defect mutation RED, and original-scenario replication.
- Sweep all live recursive teardown scans for the same disappearing-entry hazard and disposition any siblings.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A runtime experiment deterministically proves the root cause and rejects pathlib-version-only and unrelated-fixture explanations.
- [x] A gating regression test uses a deterministic synchronization barrier, reaches the disappearing-directory state, and asserts cleanup completes without masking unrelated filesystem errors.
- [x] The final-form oracle is observed RED before repair, GREEN after a held-out repair, and RED again under an exact-defect mutation.
- [x] Focused fixture/workflow tests, the broad relevant test gate, lint, and typecheck pass.
- [x] All live recursive teardown scans are audited and every confirmed sibling is fixed or ticketed.
- [x] The CI scenario no longer reproduces under repeated synchronized churn.
